doc.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Playing online concerts without an audience and closing
summary: Rowe and Baron compare performing to a camera; Baron describes the Gowanus Canal Conservancy online gala with his wife, then the interview closes.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Thank you for saying that. I experienced just a little bit of that when I got hired to do, with a bunch of other people, like, “Do a concert from your home” for a local arts center. They’re going to broadcast it. So we set up a camera.
Was that you alone or with other people online. Say it again it broke up.

Yeah by myself. So mostly I play piano also and so mostly it was that, but that feeling that we usually get, okay the song is over and we know what’s supposed to happen. We get this adulation, right? So you’re doing this film and you finish it and you look at the camera and it’s like [sighs] like nothing. And it exposes what you were saying about that, needing that adulation.

Yeah. My wife is a singer and we started doing online things. We do stuff for the local St. Mark’s Church here, part of the service every once in a while. And a friend of ours came to us, a young lady and she is part of this Gowanus Canal Conservancy and they have a big gala every year. And this year they couldn’t have it so they had it online. They asked us to perform for a half hour and then to talk a little bit about the whole Conservancy and stuff. She gave me some talking points. Now I wasn’t sure how I was going to do that without hearing people or seeing people. There were thousands of people I think were watching this. And all of a sudden I got into the groove of like knowing that people were hearing us but it was like at first it was just hard to gather some kind of instinctual way of doing this, but it worked out. My wife and I worked up some songs like “It’s a Wonderful World” and “What the World Needs Now” is love sweet love. I did “Summertime” I think by myself or something like that — oh, “Ain’t Misbehavin’” I think I did. Something like that. A couple of things by myself. And it was like the ham in me came out even though there was no one standing or sitting in front of me.

Well you keep “Ain’t Misbehavin’” or however you want to turn that around, keep behaving. And I knew this would be an informative and appropriate conversation, Art, and I’m going to stop recording but we can chat a little bit more.
All right. Thank you very much.
I’ll tell you the real story then.
